snippet.title: 영어를 길고 유창하게 말하기/듣기 연습 🎧
snippet.description:
So, I just joined a swimming class at my local sports center.
And there's this guy in the class...
I don't know if that's his way of welcoming new people
But he's been telling me a lot of stuff since day one.
But it's been mostly about the other members in the class, like,
who does what for a living, who I should watch out for - things I never asked about and some things I have no business knowing.
It wasn't until around the 3rd that I learned something.
It turned out that this guy was not getting along very well with the other people in the class.
And that's when I started to realize what he was really up to.
I think he was trying to get me on his side before I ever got to form my own opinion on everyone else.
I should've picked up on it earlier.
It's just that I've(I'd) never been in a situation like that before.
What do you call people like that?.

A: What?! That’s crazy!
B: Is it? I know the guys at HR. One of them is a guy I’ve known since high school. They’ve been trying to track Randy down for almost a year. He’s gone. Even his family doesn’t know where he is.
C: It’s aliens.
A: Excuse me?
C: It’s the only logical explanation.
He was abducted by aliens.

snippet.description:

Script : 

I remember watching this Ted talk a while back and there was this guy who gave a talk about a study that he did on successful startups and the surprising result he ended up with. The purpose of the research was to understand what led certain startups to succeed when others failed.All I remember is that he had quite a long list of companies that he targeted for the research and he had a number of factors that he used to determine the key to their success. I don't think the research was what you would call scientific or technical. But then, he must've had some recognition in his field since he was invited to give that talk. Anyway, at the end of the research, he concluded that among a number of different factors, the one that determined the success of a startup was timing more than anything else, which sounds a lot like luck if you ask me.
